title: Wittmann wins the finale and Rast takes the DTM title at the first attempt
dek: Marco Wittmann won the Hockenheim finale for BMW from third on the grid, 3.1 seconds clear of René Rast, whose second place made him champion for Audi in his first full DTM season.

chapters.title: Saturday leaves four Audis in the hunt
text: Jamie Green won Saturday's Race 1 from third on the grid, but a warning for forcing Timo Glock off the track dropped him ten places for Sunday, and Mattias Ekström, 11th without scoring, took a five-place penalty for his third warning. Ekström still led the standings on 172 points, nine ahead of Green, with René Rast on 159 and Mike Rockenfeller 20 behind the leader. The final race of the season, 55 minutes plus a lap with one mandatory stop, would decide the title among four Audi drivers.

chapters.title: Blomqvist takes the last pole of the season
text: Tom Blomqvist and Marco Wittmann fought for pole in the 20-minute session, and it was Blomqvist's BMW that came out on top with a 1:30.491. Rast, the driver who needed to beat his rivals to the title, was 0.064 seconds behind in second, with Wittmann 0.073 seconds off and Lucas Auer's Mercedes 0.088 seconds back in fourth. The pole earned Blomqvist three points and Rast's two cut his gap to Ekström to 11.

The session was stopped halfway through when a drain cover came loose on the circuit and Paul di Resta's Mercedes was damaged driving over it; the delay was a long one before the final minutes could be run. Di Resta ended up slowest of the 18 on 1:31.800.

Penalties then reshaped the grid. Green had qualified fifth, 0.099 seconds off pole, but his ten-place drop sent him to 15th, and Ekström, tenth on the road, started 14th after losing five places. Robert Wickens moved up to fifth, Maxime Martin to sixth and Rockenfeller, who had qualified eighth, to seventh. Glock, 12th fastest, started tenth.

chapters.title: Rast drops to fifth and Green to last
text: Blomqvist led away from pole and Wittmann followed, but Rast was slow off the line. Auer took the inside at Turn 1 and, as Rast tried to retake the place, Wittmann and then Wickens also got past, leaving the Audi in fifth by the end of the lap. Behind, Ekström and Green were caught up in a scramble with Maro Engel that ended with contact between the two Audis, and Green fell to the back of the field from his starting place of 15th.

Rast recovered quickly, passing Wickens on lap four or five and Auer on the main straight or at the hairpin a few laps later. With the Audi back in third behind Blomqvist and Wittmann, he was the virtual champion on the road, but Ekström and Green still had a long race ahead of them.

chapters.title: Wittmann stops first and the order reshuffles
text: Blomqvist built a small gap but lost pace and Wittmann closed on him. Wittmann and Auer stopped on lap 12, and Blomqvist came in a few laps later, after Rast had tried to pass him without success. Rast, running at the front, stopped at the end of lap 23 together with Rockenfeller, and came out second, behind Wittmann. Ekström and Green, running on a late-stop strategy, came in a lap or two after that.

Only Bruno Spengler had yet to make his mandatory stop. Around lap 25 Wickens, who had caught the cold-tyred Rast, hit the back of Blomqvist at the hairpin. The Mercedes driver was given a drive-through penalty, and the BMW, damaged at the rear, was out of the race; Wickens lost several laps and finished 17th. That left Wittmann with the lead and Rast second.

chapters.title: Ekström runs out of laps
text: The title now hung on Ekström, who needed to finish sixth or better and was gathering places after his late stop. He passed Auer and Edoardo Mortara but ran out of time, and settled for eighth. Green, who had come through the field from last place, took fifth, but he needed to be ahead of Rast to win and was not.
Rast closed on Wittmann in the closing laps without getting close enough to attack, and Rockenfeller held third. Gary Paffett was fourth, the best Mercedes.

chapters.title: Wittmann wins, Rast is champion
text: Wittmann took the flag 3.143 seconds ahead of Rast, with Rockenfeller 6.280 seconds back in third, and Paffett fourth at 15.844 seconds. Green fifth from 15th on the grid, set the fastest lap with a 1:32.456 on lap 32, and Martin, Farfus, Ekström, Mortara and Auer completed the top ten. Glock was 12th, Spengler 14th and Blomqvist, the pole-sitter, was a retirement.
It was Wittmann's first win of 2017. For Rast the second place was enough: he finished the season on 179 points, three ahead of Ekström.

chapters.title: A rookie champion and a winter of questions
text: Rast, the first driver in 24 years to win the DTM title in his debut season, finished on 179 points, three ahead of Ekström on 176 and six clear of Green on 173. Rockenfeller, who would have needed to win the race, ended up fourth in the standings on 167, 12 points behind. Audi took all three titles of the year: the drivers' championship for Rast, the teams' title for Team Rosberg, and the manufacturers' championship.

Rast said afterwards that he was not prepared for it and that he had not known at first whether he had won, calling it pure emotion and thanking Audi and Team Rosberg. His team principal, Arno Zensen, said the finish had been so tense that he almost lost his nerve, and Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass called the race a hammer. The wait lasted until the line: Ekström, who had started 14th and finished eighth, would have been champion by a point had he finished sixth.

Ekström said the team had tried everything but that it had not been enough, and congratulated Rast and Green. Green, who had started 15th and finished fifth, added that Rast had a good year and performed well overall. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz said Rast and Audi had the best package and were worthy champions, and that Paffett's fourth place was enough to secure second in the manufacturers' standings. BMW finished third.

For BMW, Wittmann's win was a high point at the end of a difficult year. He said every driver wanted to end the season with a victory, and that the team had changed the car after Saturday, which worked well. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt said three BMW drivers scored in the last race and thanked the crew for a hard year, while noting that 152,000 spectators had attended the finale weekend.

facts.v: Marco Wittmann won the final race of 2017 by 3.143 seconds from René Rast after starting third.
